full_judgment:
3. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that the respondents filed and application before the District Judge, Rajshahi on 12-9-66 for granting Letters of Administration of the Estate of late Brojendra Nath Shahs on the 'basis of a Will alleged to have been executed by him on 19-5-1965, which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1966. In view of the statement made therein that there was no near relatives of the deceased testator an order was made by the District Judge for issue of general citation fixing 11-2-67 for exparte hearing. Jogendra Nath Shaha, a full brother of Brojendra Nath Shaha coming to know of the case appeared through his constituted Attorney on 26-1-67 and opposed the prayer for granting Letters of Administration alleging inter alia that the Will was a forged one. In view of the opposition the Miscellaneous Case was re-registered as Title Suit No. 1 of 1967. The Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property, Rajshahi also appeared to contest the suit by filing a vokalatnama on 2-4-69 claiming that properties of late Brojendra Nath Shaha as enemy property had vested in the Government. The District Judge, however, by his order dated 25-4-1969 decreed the suit exparte. Against the said order the constituted Attorney of Jogendra Nath Shaha filed an appeal before the High Court on 9-7-69 being First Appeal No. 147 of 1969. The Assistant Custodian also preferred an appeal being First Appeal No. 172 of 1969. On an application for stay of execution of the exparte decree an ad-interim order of stay was made by the High Court. The civil rule for stay was made absolute on contest on 15-10-1969. On 14-8-72 the respondents, that is, the plaintiffs in the title suit, informed the Court that the appellant Jogendra Nath Shaha had died on 21-8-68. On an application for substitution of the heirs of deceased Jogendra Nath Shaha rule was issued being Civil Rule No. 847 (F) of 1972 on 21-11-72. Another application was filed in First Appeal (Probate) No. 172 of 1969 by the Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property for adding the heirs of the deceased Jogendra Nath Shaha and a rule being Civil Rule No. 484 (F) of 1972 was issued on 21-11-72. The respondents above-named appeared in both the Rules on 24-1-73 and it was stated that the appellants knew about the death of Jogendra Nath Shaha from the date of his death and not on 14-8-72 which was only the date of intimation given to the Court. The above mentioned First Appeals came up for hearing before a Division Bench on 2911-1976. The learned Judges on consideration of the facts appearing from the record dismissed both the appeals after recording the order as under:- 

 After arrival of the record to the trial Court the respondents (plaintiffs) filed an application on 27-6-77 for issue of Letters of Administration and also filed another application for revival of the Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1966. The learned District Judge by his order dated 7-7-77 rejected the application for issue of Letters of Administration but ordered that "the sued is restored to file and number." Another order was made "for issuing notice afresh on general citation and on Assistant Custodian, Enemy Property." The appellants filed an application under Order 1, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and were made parties to the case. They filed written objection contending that the suit already abated as defendant No. 1 Jogendra Nath Shaha admittedly died on 21-8-1968, that is, before the decree was passed on 25-4-69. Thereupon an issue was framed by the District Judge on the point raised by the appellant, and he by an order dated 3-1-79 held that the suit had already abated. On 4-1-79 the respondents (plaintiffs) filed an application under Order XXII, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the abatement but assigned no reason for not filing application within the prescribed time. The appellants filed written objection to the said application for setting aside abatement. Thereafter the respondents filed an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the application for setting aside the abatement. The learned District Judge, however, by his order dated 31-1-79 allowed the application and set aside the abatement of Title Suit No. 1 of 1967. On hearing the learned Counsels appearing for the parties it appears that the order of abatement was recorded by the District Judge on an erroneous view of the matter. Jogendra Nath Shaha claiming to be the only full brother of the testator appeared in the Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1966 which was converted into Title Suit No. 1 of 1967. He appeared in the matter on general citation and on his death the proceeding for Letters of Administration on the basis of a Will executed by Brojendra Nath Shaha could not abate. This aspect of the matter was neither raised by any of the parties nor considered by the learned District Judge. The First Appeal preferred by the constituted Attorney Md. Moazzem Hossain was no appeal in the eye of law in view of the fact that the principal Jogendra Nath Shaha having died his constituted Attorney ceased to have any authority to act on his behalf. The appeal preferred by the Assistant Custodian against the exparte decree was competent, but it was also erroneously dismissed and treating it as incompetent. 

 4. After arrival of the record the plaintiff-respondents filed a fresh application for granting Letters of Administration and another application for setting aside the abatement. In the application for setting aside the abatement it was stated that they were under the impression that in the instant proceedings substitution of heirs of Jogendra Nath Shaha was not necessary, and as such no application for substitution was filed, but in view of the order of abatement recorded by the Court, the application for substituting the heirs after setting aside the abatement was filed. The statement itself was sufficient for explaining the delay as contended by the appellants. However, an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condo nation of delay was filed as required by the Court. On consideration of these facts and circumstances of the case, the learned District Judge set aside the abatement with the following observation: 

 "In the peculiar circumstances of the case I like to condone the delay upto filing of the case and I hold that the application is not barred by limitation. I further hold that the plaintiffs had sufficient grounds for not substituting the heirs of Jogendra Nath Shaha within the period of limitation. Accordingly, the application is liable to be allowed and the abatement is due to be set aside.''
